newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB appoints Kellogg executive as new MD.
newsitem.headline: AWB appoints Kellogg executive as new MD.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Wednesday it had appointed Murray Rogers, executive chairman of Kellogg Australia, as its new managing director. Kellogg Australia is a unit of Kellogg Co.
Rogers will replace former AWB managing director John Lawrenson, who has been with the board for seven years.
Flugge said Rogers would lead the AWB through a major period of change, which will involve a government competition policy review in 1999.
The main focus of the review will be whether the AWB is allowed to retain its successful monopoly on Australian wheat export sales.
Australia's minister for primiary industry John Anderson on Thursday would announce a broad restructuring of the AWB which would include a corporate model, Flugge said.
This would move the AWB from a statutory authority to a private grower-owned company, which was more than likely to list on the Australian stock exchange after year 2000, he said.
Internal changes involving the relationship between growers and customers at the AWB were also under review, Flugge said.
"Murray will be leading and driving that process over the next 12 months, " Flugge said.
"The business is now very large and very complex," Flugge said.

The AWB would export 20.2 million tonnes of wheat worth about A$4.0 billion in the year to September 30 1997, Flugge said. It borrowed about A$3 billion a year for initial payments to growers and controlled about 70 percent of the domestic wheat market, he said.
Flugge also predicted the AWB's relationship with Japan's Zennoh group, a huge farmers co-operative, would grow strongly as part of the AWB's widening of its international linkages.
